chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Abil Qasim al-Kufy, on the authority of Abdul-Mumin al-Ansari, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'I have cursed seven [groups]; God and all the Prophets whose prayers are answered before me have also cursed them.' It was asked, 'Who are they?' He said: 'The one who adds to the Book of God, the one who denies Divine Destiny, the one who opposes my Sunnah, the one who considers lawful from my Itrat what God has forbidden, the one who comes into power by force so as to debase those whom God has debased and to debase those whom God has honored, the one who monopolizes the war booty of the Muslims considering it lawful, and the one who forbids what God, the Exalted, has made lawful.'

key_terms.الزَّائِدُ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: The one who adds to the Quran

ai.seo_question: Who are the seven groups cursed by the Prophet and God in al-Khisal?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith outlines seven specific groups cursed by the Prophet and God, emphasizing their theological and political deviations. Notably, the curse on those who 'misuse the Ahl al-Bayt' (al-mustahl min ‘itrati) highlights the unique status of the Prophet's family, while the reference to 'destiny' (qadar) reflects early Shia debates on divine decree versus human agency. This enumeration serves as a foundational critique of opposing sects and caliphal authorities in Shia historiography.
